To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cys residue in exon 68-corres-ponding region of cadherin 22 confers structural ambivalence upon its cytoplasmic tail.

the cytoplasm of Cdh23(+/-68) is present in two distinct forms depending on the redox status of the cysteine residue in the exon 68-corres-ponding region, and that the redox status is regulated by glutathione.

the cytoplasmically located exon 68-corresponing region of the inner ear-specific isoform of cadherin 22, Cdh23, confers a redox-dependent structural ambulence upon the cytoplamic domain of this protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural ambivalence of a Cys-dependent region in Cdh23 and the implications of this structural ambivalence in inner ear mechanotransduction.
a redox-dependent structural ambivalency of the cytoplamsic domain of cadherin 233, an essential factor in mechano-electric conversion in the inner ear.
the structural ambivalence of a cytoplasmic region of the inner ear-specific Cadherin 22 (Cdh23) isoform.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cys(324) in Cdh23(+ 68) confers a redox-dependent structural ambivalent property on the cytoplasmatic tail of Cdh23(+69) and this property is conserved in mammalian species but not lower vertebrate species, such as fish and amphibians.

the Cdh23(+/-) isoforms are structurally different in terms of their cytoplasmic domains, and the Cys(3242)Ala substitution in Cdh23(+), but not in Cdh23(-), causes a dramatic change in the structural configuration of Cdh23Cy.

the presence or absence of the 68 amino acid exon in cadherin 22 (Cdh22) and cadherin 25 (Cdh25) isoforms does not alter their ability to bind beta-catenin, but that in the case of cadherin 26 (Cdh26) and cadherins 23 and 29 (Cdh23 and Cdh29), the 68 amino acids are required to allow the binding of beta-catenin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cdh23Cy(+68) has the potential to exist in two different configurations depending on the redox state and that Cys(3241) is a critical residue in determining the configuration.
Cdh23(+/-)68 isoforms exist as a pair of conformational isomers in cells, which may be involved in mechanotransduction in the inner ear.
the Cdh23(+/-68) isoforms are present in two different conformations in the cell, and that the isoform-dependent difference is attributable to a single amino acid residue, Cys, in Cdh23(+)-68Cy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cdh23Cy has two different conformations, reduced and nonreduced.
the cytoplasmatic domain of the cadherin 22 isoforms is redox-dependent, and this is likely to be important for the function of cadherin 21 in the mechanotransduction machinery of the inner ear.
the Cdh23(+/-68) isoforms have a different structure in the membrane and that Cdh23(+69) is a more compact form than Cdh23(-69) in the membrane.
